plan_a_advantages: More emphasis on aerobic endurance development through longer, easy runs.
Includes a dedicated interval session to improve threshold power, a key component of trail running speed.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates strength training, which can be helpful for hill climbing.
Includes varied cross-training, potentially offering a broader range of fitness benefits beyond just running.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes building a strong aerobic base through consistent, longer runs at an easy pace, alongside a single, well-structured interval session to develop threshold power – crucial for trail running's varied terrain. Plan B, while including some tempo work, leans heavily into strength training and cross-training, which, while beneficial, aren't the primary drivers of speed in trail running. Plan A’s focus on sustained aerobic effort and trail-specific volume will more directly translate to improved running efficiency and speed on the trails.
